correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated all 16,777,216 states from the frozen edge list with the synchronous bit-plane update; checked its transition on a separate scalar implementation and verified the 18-edge relabelling to LCF. The full image of F^32 contains exactly 4,159 states and I verified that F permutes this image, proving that it consists precisely of all periodic states. Cycle tracing on the image gives least periods and orbit labels. The F^32 image of each start determines its basin; iterative preimages of the periodic set give exact first-entry layers. The replay matches all 72 nonempty histogram cells, orbit counts (1,1024,10,2) at periods (1,4,5,6), all period basin totals and maximum entry times, the listed individual sizes at periods 5 and 6, and the range from 9 to 373631 at period 4. The strict comparison is 385193>373631. Exactly 18 starts first enter at 27, all with period 4; witness 5999879 first repeats at step 31, returning to state 3222501 first reached at 27. The lcm of the periods is 60, so F^87=F^27 follows. This exhaustive method does not use either supplied C++ enumerator or its output to construct the census.
residual_risks: Census applies only to this graph and simultaneous four-state threshold-one rule. The archived C++ reports summarize period-4 basin sizes with count, range and total, not a raw list of 1024 sizes; that suffices for the frozen inequality and table and is not evidence of a cellwise printed basin list.

Resultary same-graph three-state and nearby four-state comparisons
value.rationale: The canonical asymmetric cubic graph is a motivated finite test of excitable dynamics without nontrivial graph automorphisms. The full entry-time/period law and sharp uniform cutoff are useful exact benchmarks. More specifically, period counts favor four-cycles 1024 to 10 while every period-five orbit individually beats every period-four orbit in basin weight. This is a structural separation about uniformly sampled starts that could not be read off from recurrent-state counts or an aggregate comparison.
residual_risks: The result does not explain the basin separation via a general mechanism or imply a pattern across graphs or refractory counts.
